Hannah / Kim / Alice — attaching the artifacts we discussed. Attachments: network_demarcation_diagram_v2.png, operator_runbook_snapshot.pdf, segregation_evidence.zip (redacted logs and config snapshots).

High-level summary (for Orchid review):

- Isolation model: each tenant is pinned to a logical pool (tenant slice) with dedicated inference workers. The control plane (model registry, routing, orchestration) runs in a separate management tier with strict mTLS and role-based access. Per-tenant requests traverse a sidecar that enforces per-tenant egress allowlist and prefix/KV cache scoping.

- Control-plane/data-plane demarcation: control-plane APIs live on a private network segment accessible only to operator-management subnets and customer-dedicated proxies. The data plane (inference workers + sidecars) only accepts inbound inference requests and RTC token exchange; it does not initiate arbitrary outbound control-plane calls. Outbound control-plane calls are restricted by egress policies to a small set of internal endpoints (registry, telemetry ingest, KMS).

- Failure modes and mitigations (short):
  * Sidecar failure (runtime crash or OOM): automated restart via our runtime supervisor, request-level circuit breaker that routes to a hot-spare pool; graceful degradation to a compatible model variant. See diagram legend for flow.
  * KV-cache poisoning / corruption: cache writes are append-only with checksums; critical cache state is backed by a versioned backing store; we detect divergence via integrity probes and auto-fall back to a cold-cache retrieval path while signaling operator alert.
  * Inter-zone partition: smart routing shifts traffic to healthy zones based on latency SLOs, and we fall back to a read-only control-plane shim for management commands until reconciliation. Rollback playbooks included in operator_runbook_snapshot.pdf.

- Egress & third-party dependencies: outbound egress from data-plane is limited to: (1) internal telemetry collectors, (2) KMS endpoints (customer KMS is optional), and (3) optional artifact registries for model pulls. We do not rely on third-party CDN for inference traffic; observability exports may optionally use vendor telemetry destinations — those are configurable per-customer and require explicit allowlisting. Evidence of egress rules and ip allowlists included in segregation_evidence.zip.

- Audit/telemetry: included sample trace snippets (redacted) and config snapshots showing egress ACLs, bootstrapping sequence, and operator runbook excerpts.

Drive link with editable Visio/PNG: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3c_RFP-OrchidBank

Ben / Hannah — this is great, thanks for the quick turnaround and the artifacts. A couple quick clarifications before we include in the board packet:

1) When you say "control-plane APIs live on a private network segment" — can you confirm whether operator access requires a bastion or if you rely on per-operator short-lived credentials + proxy? Our audit team prefers bastion-mediated operator sessions where possible.

2) For telemetry exports: you mentioned optional vendor destinations. Which vendors do customers commonly pick and how is PII redaction enforced before export?

If you can reply with two short bullets for each item we will fold into the appendix. Otherwise this is good to go.

Best,
Alice
Head of Infrastructure Security — Orchid Bank
